items.title: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels since Nepal-Tibet floods

children.content: Rescuers are racing to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites since last week's catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border, as the death toll passes 950 with more than 4,400 people missing.

image.altText: Rescue workers and army personnel at the opening of a large tunnel

items.title: Jury finds ex-gang leader guilty in Tupac Shakur killing case

children.content: A Las Vegas jury has found a former gang leader guilty of murder in a case accusing him of masterminding the drive-by 1996 killing of legendary hip-hop artist Tupac Shakur.

image.altText: Tupac Shakur

items.title: Labor rebukes Hanson claim PM 'crossed a line' with criticism

children.content: Attorney-General Michelle Rowland has urged Pauline Hanson to reflect on her own actions after the One Nation leader accused the prime minister of crossing a line in his criticism of the minor party. Follow live.

image.altText: Pauline Hanson stands in a corridor with a smile on her face.

items.title: Scandal-plagued KPMG starts to pay the bill for its mistakes

children.content: In the wake of scandals about the misuse of confidential information, embattled consulting firm KPMG is losing million-dollar contracts and cutting its workforce. And that's all before the corporate regulator, ASIC, has even opened its mouth.

image.altText: A logo on top of a building with white letters that read KPMG with a blue background.

avatar.alt: ABC business reporter Daniel Ziffer in a front on profile shot wearing a grey suit and stripy tie.

items.title: Luxury villas allegedly installed without permission in bushfire-prone area

children.content: Luxury tourist villas being offered for hundreds of dollars a night were allegedly installed in a bushfire-prone area without prior permission, an ABC investigation has found.

items.title: Oil prices surge on latest US-Iran flare-up, ASX to slip as housing slump continues

children.content: The latest flare-up in hostilities between the US and Iran have led to a 3 per cent surge in the oil price. The Australian share market is likely to start its day lower. House prices are falling in most of the nation's capital cities. Follow the day's events on the ABC News live markets blog.

image.altText: ASX

items.title: Police investigate online posts after man killed in Sydney home invasion

children.content: A man believed to be in his 20s has been shot dead during a "targeted" home invasion south-west of Sydney, police say.

image.altText: Police in white suits inside light brick home with light-coloured features, police van in front of the car

items.title: Housing downturn accelerates as 93pc of capital city suburbs record decline

children.content: Australian house prices have fallen for a fifth straight month, according to property data firm Cotality. It says the downturn has now spread to 93 per cent of suburbs in the nation's capital cities.

image.altText: Aerial shot of dozens of houses in neat rows in a new outer-suburban housing estate.

items.title: China warns Pacific nations of 'consequences' for Taiwan forum invite

children.content: There are concerns tensions between China and Taiwan could explode into the open at this year's meeting, distracting from the key Pacific priorities.

children.content: Lionel Messi ends his international football career as a living legend with a God-like status in his country, but the dizzying heights the great man reached almost never happened if he had stuck to his original retirement.

items.title: 'Canberrans suing their own government' costing ACT tens of millions

children.content: The ACT government paid out more than $60 millions in damages, settlements, and legal costs for medical negligence claims in the 2025-26 financial year, more than double the same costs in 2023-24.

image.altText: A monitor in a hospital room seen from outside.

items.title: Eight years after giving birth, mother's body is still healing

children.content: Vaginal birth is the biggest risk factor for pelvic organ prolapse, but experts say women are not being told about the risks and warning signs prior to birth. It comes as wait times for surgeries continue to grow.

image.altText: A woman holds a young boy and smiles.

items.title: New pressure on PM to allow telehealth for voluntary assisted dying

children.content: South Australia has become the first state to formally urge the Commonwealth to change a federal law preventing doctors from using telehealth in voluntary assisted dying (VAD).

image.altText: A young girl's hand over an elderly man's hand sitting on the arm of a chair.

items.title: Facial recognition technology 'scope creep' is upon us, experts warn

children.content: Industry groups say the move to facial scans in supermarkets is about safety, but analysts say that once the technology is installed, its "scope creep" paves the way for options like discriminatory pricing.

items.title: Proposal for public walkway around waterside mansions survives vote
